pointers.sentence: 6.1 came out on 5 August 2026, the day after 5.2.17 and 6.0.8 (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`), with a patch for each fix of that day, the security archive says (`docs/releases/security.txt`), and 6.1.1 lists no security fix.

6.1 came out on 5 August 2026, the day after 5.2.17 and 6.0.8 (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`), with a patch for each fix of that day, the security archive says (`docs/releases/security.txt`), and 6.1.1 lists no security fix.
`UpdateCacheMiddleware.process_response`, which `cache_page` runs too, returns a response unstored at the first check that holds (`django/middleware/cache.py:UpdateCacheMiddleware.process_response`).

`SessionMiddleware.process_response` now adds `"Cookie"` to `"Vary"` whenever it sets or deletes the cookie, and when the session was read (`django/contrib/sessions/middleware.py:SessionMiddleware.process_response`; [`SessionMiddleware`: the cookie and the save](../auth/session-middleware.md)).

Cache-Control's `"private"`, `"no-cache"` and `"no-store"` are found whatever their case, where only a lower-case private used to be (CVE-2026-8404; 5.2.15, 6.0.6), and with a value, as `private="Set-Cookie"` (`django/utils/http.py:split_directive_names`).

A `"Vary"` of `"*"` used to be stored (CVE-2026-6907; 5.2.14, 6.0.5), as did a star with white space around it (CVE-2026-48587; 5.2.15, 6.0.6); `has_vary_header` now compares stripped names (`django/utils/cache.py:has_vary_header`).

It writes a header into `HttpRequest.META` as WSGI does, its hyphens as underscores, so a header sent as x_forwarded_for, which a proxy stripping X-Forwarded-For let through, landed on X-Forwarded-For's key (`django/core/handlers/asgi.py:ASGIRequest.__init__`; [Making the request: `WSGIRequest` and `ASGIRequest`](../http/request.md#from-an-asgi-scope)).

`DomainNameValidator` refuses a value with a newline in it (CVE-2026-53878; 5.2.16, 6.0.7): its pattern ends at `"\Z"`, where `"$"` would match before a final newline (`django/core/validators.py:DomainNameValidator.__init__`; [Validators: `django/core/validators.py`](../forms/validators.md)).

`DomainNameValidator` refuses a value with a newline in it (CVE-2026-53878; 5.2.16, 6.0.7): its pattern ends at `"\Z"`, where `"$"` would match before a final newline (`django/core/validators.py:DomainNameValidator.__init__`; [Validators: `django/core/validators.py`](../forms/validators.md)).
A newline let through could inject a header into a response, though `HttpResponse` refuses one in a header (`django/http/response.py:ResponseHeaders._convert_to_charset`).
At this commit `log_message` does it for `log_response` (`django/utils/log.py:log_message`; [Logging](../startup/logging.md)).

Since 6.0 `WSGIRequestHandler.log_message` hands its arguments to `log_message` (`django/core/servers/basehttp.py:WSGIRequestHandler.log_message`; [The development server](../commands/runserver.md)); no 6.0 note lists the change.

`ModelBackend.authenticate` hands the user, or `None`, to `check_password_with_timing_attack_mitigation`, which hashes for nothing when there is none (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:check_password_with_timing_attack_mitigation`; [Authenticating: `authenticate` and the backends](../auth/authenticating.md)).

An unusable password ran no hasher, and so told its user apart (CVE-2024-39329; 5.0.7); `verify_password` now hashes random characters when the stored password is unusable or its hasher unknown, or the password given is `None` (`django/contrib/auth/hashers.py:verify_password`).
The mod_wsgi handler hashed nothing for a name with no account (CVE-2025-13473; 5.2.11, 6.0.2), and at this commit calls the same function (`django/contrib/auth/handlers/modwsgi.py:check_password`).

A password reset whose mail failed raised, and so showed whether an address had an account (CVE-2024-45231; 5.0.9, 5.1.1); `PasswordResetForm.send_mail` now logs the failure to `"django.contrib.auth"` (`django/contrib/auth/forms.py:PasswordResetForm.send_mail`; [Password reset: `PasswordResetTokenGenerator` and the reset views](../auth/password-reset.md)).

`Storage.save` checks a name with `validate_file_name` as it arrives, after `Storage.get_available_name` and after `_save`, refusing an absolute name or one with `".."` among its parts (`django/core/files/storage/base.py:Storage.save`; [File storage: `Storage`, `FileSystemStorage` and `storages`](../services/storage.md)).

`extract`, which startproject and startapp use for a template archive, refuses a member unless `os.path.commonpath` of its path and the target is the target (`django/utils/archive.py:BaseArchive.target_filename`; [Paths and archives: `safe_join`, `safe_makedirs` and `extract`](../utils/paths.md)); a member bound for a sibling whose name begins with the target's used to pass (CVE-2025-59682; 5.1.13, 5.2.7).

`FileSystemStorage`, given a mode for directories, and `FileBasedCache` make them through `safe_makedirs` and so `makedirs`, which sets each mode with `os.chmod` after `os.mkdir` (`django/utils/_os.py:makedirs`).

`GenericInlineModelAdmin.get_formset` gives its forms a `BaseForm.has_changed` that answers false for a new row the user may not add and for an existing one they may not change, as `InlineModelAdmin.get_formset` does (CVE-2026-4277; 5.2.13, 6.0.4) (`django/contrib/contenttypes/admin.py:GenericInlineModelAdmin.get_formset`; [Inlines: `InlineModelAdmin` and its formsets](../admin/inlines.md)).

`ModelAdmin.list_editable`'s formset could create rows; `ModelAdmin._save_formset` raises `BadRequest` for a changed form whose object is new (CVE-2026-4292; 5.2.13, 6.0.4) (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin._save_formset`; [The change list's columns: `list_display` and `list_editable`](../admin/list-display.md)).

`display_for_field` makes a model's URL field a link only if `URLValidator` accepts the value, whatever the field's own validators allow (`django/contrib/admin/utils.py:display_for_field`); a value with a dangerous scheme was a link (CVE-2026-15920; 5.2.17, 6.0.8).
The salt now carries a prefix and the given salt's length (`django/core/signing.py:_cookie_signer_salt`).

A cookie signed with the old salt is still read while the setting `SIGNED_COOKIE_LEGACY_SALT_FALLBACK` is true, its default until 6.1 (`django/core/signing.py:_unsign_cookie`; [What changed in security: Content Security Policy and signing](security.md)).

`EmailBackend.open` now makes a new connection the backend's only once STARTTLS and the login have succeeded (`django/core/mail/backends/smtp.py:EmailBackend.open`; [Sending email: `mailers` and the email backends](../services/mailers.md)).

`GDALRaster.check_raster_lookup_value` refuses a dictionary, a string or a path with `DisallowedRasterLookup`, a `SuspiciousOperation` (`django/contrib/gis/gdal/raster/source.py:GDALRaster.check_raster_lookup_value`).
A `GDALRaster` passes (`django/contrib/gis/db/models/fields.py:BaseSpatialField.get_prep_value`; [Spatial fields: the geometry fields and `RasterField`](../contrib/spatial-fields.md)).

A `GDALRaster` made from bytes gives its in-memory file exactly their length, which `GDALRaster.vsi_buffer` reads back; it read some 32 bytes past the buffer (CVE-2026-53877; 5.2.16, 6.0.7) (`django/contrib/gis/gdal/raster/source.py:GDALRaster.__init__`).
